action_regex_regex_help:
A regex expression to match the input.

If you use group names in the regex expression Tasker will create a variable for each of those groups. That variable can be accessed either as direct value or as an array if multiple matches are found.
array_join_formatter_help:
Will merge each position of the arrays above with the format you specify here.

Use the original array name as the placeholder in the format

For example, if you have 2 arrays, %names and %ages and use the fomat '%names is %ages years old' it'll join 
'%names(1) is %ages(1) years old'
'%names(2) is %ages(2) years old'
and so on.
array_join_output_help:
Name of the array that will contain the formatted values.

Each position of this array will contain the corresponding positions of all the input arrays joined with the rules above.
array_join_output_joiner_help: If set, will join the resulting array and make the output variable a single value instead of an array.
array_joiner_help:
Will simply merge each position of the arrays above with the joiner.

For example, if you have 2 arrays, %names and %ages and use the joiner ' - ' it'll join '%names(1) - %ages(1)', '%names(2) - %ages(2)' and so on.
array_merge_replace_variables_in_arrays_: If enabled, Tasker will not only replace the array items themselves in, but it will look INSIDE those array items and replace any variables there too.
call_reject_help: Prevent call from going through and disconnects it as if the user had manually rejected it
call_silence_help: Sets whether ringing should be silenced for the incoming call but call will still go through.
call_skip_log_help: Prevent call from going through and make the call not appear in your call log
clipboard_image_help: Setting an image on the clipboard will overwrite the text above
convert_orientation_help: If enabled will convert orientation values to degrees. Result must have at least 3 values for this to work.
dc_collision_help:
What to do when another copy of this task is already executing.

See the page on Tasks in the Userguide for more information.
dc_delete_on_disable_help: Whether this profile should be deleted when the repeat count gets to 0.
dc_element_geom_help:
Allows more precise specification of the element's position (x,y) and size (width x height) than is possible via finger adjustment.

There is a separate geometry specification for each display orientation (portrait and landscape).
dc_enforce_task_order_help: Ensure that tasks resulting from this profile activation or deactivation remain queued until previous tasks from this profile are complete.
dc_insert_your_google_api_key_check_help: Insert your Google API Key. Check the action's help page for more info.
dc_licence_help: For customers who purchased a direct-download key on or after July 2018:
dc_limit_repeats_help: Whether to limit the number of times the profile can become active e.g. if its enter task should only be run once.
dc_limit_repeats_to_help: The number of times remaining before this profile becomes disabled.
dc_profile_cooldown_help:
The times after the profile has become active before it can again become active.

Cooldown time is reset after a reboot.
dc_profile_priority_help:
The priority of the enter and exit tasks run by this profile.

Note: this does *not* affect the profile becoming active in any way.
dc_profile_properties_restore_settings_h:
Whether to automatically restore the values of any settings (actions marked with a double arrow symbol) changed by this profile when it deactivates.

See also: Settings in the Userguide.
dc_run_exit_on_startup_if_not_active_hel: If this option is enabled, when Tasker starts up (after a reboot for example) the exit task for this profile will be ran if the profile's condition doesn't match your current situation, ie. the profile is not active
dc_show_notification_help_help:
Whether to include this task in the Running Tasks notification that updates every time a task is started or stopped.

You can disable the notification altogether by long-clicking it and changing its settings.
dc_stay_awake_help:
Whether to keep the device running while the task is running. The default is that tasks will be guaranteed to be kept running for around a minute from their start time.

Be careful specifying this option for a task with a loop, it can very quickly drain your battery.
dc_widget_task_priority_help: The priority at which the widget/shortcut task will be launched.
help_adb_wifi_enable_debugging:
Most people don't need debugging to be enabled at all times on their Android devices. It might be a security risk if you accidentally accept an unknown request to start debugging which could put your phone at risk.

By enabling this option you can leave debugging off and the action will enable it when ran and disable it afterwards, leaving your phone "closed down" for the majority of time!
help_adb_wifi_result_encoding:
If you are expecting a result with non-standard characters (like à or é) you can use a different encoding for the result.

Try using 'UTF-8' (no quotes) in situations like this, for example.
help_allow_child_overwrite_vars:
If enabled the child task is free to overwrite any variables that already exist in this parent task.

Please note that you need to enable the option to replace in the 'Return' action as well.

This option is meant to be used with child tasks that you know yourself and not any random child tasks.

Please be aware that if you enable this, child tasks can change the parents local and Project/Profile/Task variables even if Local Variable Passthrough is not checked and the contents of the parent's variables are not visible to the child task.
help_allow_scene_outside_boundaries:
If enabled, will allow the scene to be shown outside normal UI boundaries.

This is necessary to display overlays on the status bar on phones with notches, or on the navigation bar for example.

To display scenes outside boundaries, manually enter the horizontal and vertical positions (using the cross-arrow button on each field) and input appropriate values, including negative ones.

When using this mode any values entered manually (instead of using the seek control) will be in pixels instead of the normal 0-200 range to allow more fine-grained control.
help_contact_via_app_backout: When enabled, will back out of the opened WhatsApp conversation so you end up where you were before the conversation was opened.
help_go_home_package:
This will not change your default launcher. It will simply launch it once. If you touch the home button your default launcher will be opened.

If you want to change the default launcher check out the ADB Wifi action.
help_interactive_out_of_bounds_scenes:
If the Tasker Accessibility Service is enabled when this scene is created and you enable the 'Blocking Overlay +' option below, you'll be able to interact with the scene even if it is on the status bar or navigation bar, meaning that you can create custom buttons for your navigation bar for example!

These scenes will also show on your lock screen and some Always-On-Displays (depending on your phone) and can be interacted with on the lock screen even if the phone is locked!
help_limit_passthrough:
Either a Tasker pattern or a comma separated list to limit which variables can go through.

Local variables that do not match the pattern or comma separated list will not be available in the other task.
help_local_variable_passthrough_limit:
A comma separated list of variable names (including the %) that represent the variables that you want to pass through to the other task.

Other local variables will not be available in the other task.
help_notify_plain_icon_can_be_anything:
The notification icon that shows in the status bar at the top of your display.

This icon can be any built-in icon, local file, URL or even just some text.

For example, you could create a notification with '26º' set as the icon and that text would appear on your status bar.
help_notify_plain_live_update:
Only available on Android 16+.

Will only show if Tasker is not the foreground app.

Live Update notifications appear more prominently on system surfaces, including at the top of the notification drawer and the lock screen, and as a chip in the status bar.
help_notify_short_critical_text:
Only available on Android 16+.

Will only show if Tasker is not the foreground app.

Sets a very short string summarizing the most critical information contained in the notification. Suggested max length is 7 characters, and there is no guarantee how much or how little of this text will be shown.

If shown, will appear in the Notification Icon Chip if 'Live Update' is enabled, and only if Tasker is not in the foreground.
help_perform_task_passthrough: If enabled all the variables that are available in this task will also be available in the child task according to the restrictions below.
help_pick_input_text: Will appear in the dialog if the title is also set
help_pick_input_title: If set will make a dialog appear prior to picking the input with the title and text, unless the specific input picker has a place for the title (like the Time dialog for example).
help_pick_matter_device:
You can control multiple devices in a single action using Tasker's Pattern Matching.

For example, if you have a light called 'Ceiling 1' and another one called 'Ceiling 2', you can toggle them both by setting the name to 'Ceiling *'.

All options bellow will apply to all matching devices.
help_progress_action:
Whether to show/update a progress dialog or to hide an existing one.

If you choose to hide the dialog but the dialog isn't showing the action will end successfully right away.
help_progress_animation_frame_duration: The time in milliseconds that each image appears on the screen
help_progress_animation_images: A list of images to use as an animation in the dialog.
help_progress_animation_tint:
This will tint the images with the selected color where they are not transparent.

By default this is set to Tasker's accent color
help_progress_title_text:
You must set this if the dialog isn't already showing.

If it's already showing you can omit this and the last used value will be kept.
help_progress_type: You can either show a looping animation if you don't have a numeric progress to report, or show a progress bar where you can show numerical progress.
help_return_passthrough: If enabled all the variables that are available in this task will also be available in the parent task according to the restrictions below.
help_return_passthrough_list: If you only want to send a few variables back to the parent task, insert a / separated list of those variable names here.
help_return_passthrough_replace:
If this is not enabled, variables that already have a value on the parent task will not be replaced by their values in this task.

Please note that you need to enable the option to allow replacements in the 'Perform Task' action as well.
help_run_shell_use_shizuku:
You can run a command with Shizuku, meaning that the command will use whatever privileges Shizuku has on your device.

To use this, the Shizuku service has to be running and Tasker has to have the Shizuku permission enabled.
help_run_shell_use_tasker_settings:
Since Tasker started targeting API 30 some shell commands (like "ip neigh") stopped working.

Use this option to use the Tasker Settings app to run the command instead of it running directly in Tasker.
help_screen_capture_mode:
You can either start, stop or query a screen capture.

Starting a capture when it's already started will result in an error.

Stopping a capture when it's already stopped will result in an error.

Use 'Query' to know if a capture is currently ongoing or not (check the %sc_is_capturing variable).
help_set_quick_tile_command:
An optional Tasker command that will be sent on tap.

You can react to this command in a profile with the 'Tasker Command' event condition.
help_set_quick_tile_command_prefix:
If set, instead of just sending the commands set above, all commands will be prefixed with the prefix set here followed by '=:='.

For example, if you set the regular command to 'short', the long click command to 'long' and the prefix to 'quick', on normal tap the 'quick=:=short' command will be sent and on long tap the 'quick=:=long' command will be sent.
help_set_quick_tile_icon:
The icon for the quick setting tile.

If not set, the task's icon will be used instead.

You can also use any text characters as it'll use that as an icon although be aware that at max only 1 or 2 characters will fit in the small icon's size.
help_set_quick_tile_label:
The label for the quick setting tile.

If not set, the task's name will be used instead.
help_show_on_lock_screen_everywhere:
Will make an overlay scene show on the lock screen and over the notification tray.

If you run this action with this option enabled and the Tasker accessibility service is not running an error notification will be shown and the action will error out.
help_show_on_lock_screen_interactive_eve:
Will make an overlay scene show (and be interactive) on the lock screen and on some devices even in the Always-On-Display.

It'll also make scenes clickable even if they are on the status or notification bars

If you run this action with this option enabled and the Tasker accessibility service is not running an error notification will be shown and the action will error out.

Useful if you want to show a blocking overlay that is interactive even if on the status/navigation bar and lock screen.

If this option is not enabled the scene will not show on the lock screen and won't be clickable if it's over the status/navigation bar.
help_text_dialog_image: If set, will show an image between the title and text
help_text_dialog_image_max_size:
Size in dip (density-independent pixels). If an image is set you can optionally limit its size with this.

Original image proportions will always be respected.
help_toast_background_color:
Color for the background of the toast.

If not set the current Tasker theme background color will be used.
help_toast_command:
If set, will make the toast interactive and when clicked will call the chosen task.

All the variables available in the task where the toast is created will also be available in the called task.
help_toast_continue_task_right_away: If disabled, will not advance the task to the next action until the toast is gone from the screen.
help_toast_hide_on_click: If enabled, will make the flash go away as soon as it's clicked and the task is launched.
help_toast_icon:
Icon to show on the toast.

If not set, no icon will be shown at all.
help_toast_icon_size:
Size of the icon in dip (density-independent pixels).

Default value is 24.
help_toast_id:
If you set an ID and an existing flash is already showing with the same ID, it'll be replaced by the new one.

If no ID is set, they will appear on top of each other.
help_toast_position:
One of TopLeft, Top, TopRight, Right, BottomRight, Bottom, BottomLeft or Left.

Can optionally provide an offset in dip separated by a comma from the position.

Use the helper for easier setup.
help_toast_show_over_everything:
If enabled, will make the toast show over system UI like the notification tray, lock screen, or even AOD on some devices.

Tasker's accessibility service needs to be on for this to work.

If you want you can disable the 'Continue Task Immediately' option and Tasker will toggle the service on and off when needed automatically.
help_toast_tasker_layout:
Will show the text in a custom Tasker toast instead of using a normal system toast.

You can use HTML to format your text when this option is enabled. For example, you can use <font color=red>Some Text</font> to show some text in red.

Useful to get advanced toast functionality or if your device doesn't support multi-line toasts for example.
help_toast_text_color:
Color for the text of the toast.

If not set, an appropriate text color for the background color will be chosen so that it has good contrast.

If HTML is used in the text and color is sent that way, it'll override this setting just for those parts of the text.
help_toast_timeout_override:
Time in milliseconds the toast should appear on the screen.

If set Will override the normal 'Long' setting above.
help_toast_title: Title to show up above the normal toast text. If not set, only the text will show.
help_toggle_profile:
You can only enable/disable profiles that you have explicitly given a name to.

If a profile isn't showing up here go to your profile list, long click on the profile and give it a name.
help_variable_map_input: The input value that you want to map to the output range based on the input range.
help_widgetv2_ask_to_add: If the widget is not already added to your home screen, show a popup asking you to add it.
help_widgetv2_background_color:
The background color of the whole widget.

If you don't specify text color, it'll automatically be chosen to contrast with this.
help_widgetv2_command_prefix: If set, will prepend "prefix=:=" to all your commands above (where "prefix" is the actual prefix you specify here).
help_widgetv2_commands:
Commands to be ran when you tap on the texts/images above.

Specify one command for each of the text/image, or leave blank to make them not clickable.

These commands will trigger the 'Command' event in Tasker. Check that for more info.
help_widgetv2_custom_layout:
Specify your custom layout here as a JSON structure.

You can also directly use an HTTP/S URL or a file path here.

Make sure to escape any variables you are using inside JSON strings with the 'Variable Convert' action > 'JSON Encode' if needed.

Click below to learn all about Custom Layouts.
help_widgetv2_image_tints:
If you set this, you'll colorize the images above with a single, solid color.

You can specify an image not to be tinted by leaving the value empty.

If you specify less colors than images, the last specified colour will be used for the remainder of the images.
help_widgetv2_images:
Depending on the chosen layout, these images can appear in different places:

- Buttons: are used as the main image for each button
- Media: the first image will be used as the main one on the left. The rest are used as buttons below.
help_widgetv2_material_you_colors: If enabled, will use Material You colors whenever colors are not set explicitly above, which means, the Widget colors will match your wallpaper.
help_widgetv2_number_of_columns:
The number of columns the widget will have to show your data.

For example, if you specify 10 texts and set Number of Columns to 5, you'll get 2 rows with 5 columns each.
help_widgetv2_sizes:
The size or sizes you want the images to have in dp (Density Independent Pixels).

If you specify less sizes than images, the last specified size will be used for the remainder of the images.
help_widgetv2_tasks:
Tasks to be ran when you tap on the texts/images above.

Specify one task for each of the text/image, or leave blank to make them not clickable.
help_widgetv2_text:
Depending on the chosen layout, these texts can appear in different places:

- Buttons: are used as labels for each button
- Media: is used as the subtitle for the widget
help_widgetv2_text_styles:
Styles for each of the texts above.

If you specify less styles than texts, the last specified style will be used for the remainder of the texts.

A style can be:

- a color in HTML notation or one of the color Material Design tokens (primary, onPrimary, secondary, etc) 
- a number to set the text size in sp
- one of 'sansserif', 'serif', 'monospace', 'cursive' to set the font family
- one of 'left', 'right', 'center', 'start', 'end' to set text alignment
-italic
-bold
-underline
-linethrough

For example, you could set 2 texts with 2 different styles:
- Red, bold text
- Green, italic, underlined text

by setting this to

#FF0000 bold,#00FF00 italic underline.

IMPORTANT: Keep in mind that the title also counts as a text, so the first style you provide is assigned to the title.
ignore_tasker_sets_help: If selected this event will not trigger if Tasker was the app that set the clipboard
input_dates_format_help:
One or more date formats.

For example, yyyy/MM/dd HH:mm will correctly parse a date like 2021/03/05 14:18

You can use a different format for each input.

If there are more inputs than formats, the last format on the list will be used for the remainder of the inputs.
input_dates_help:
One or more dates.

Can be direct values, values from variables or even direct arrays (use %array, not %array()).
java_code_use_tasker_settings_help:
Access a Broader Range of Android APIs

Google Play requires Tasker to be built for recent Android versions (a high 'Target API'). This enhances security but limits access to certain developer functions (APIs).

By checking this, your Java code will be executed by the 'Tasker Settings' app. 'Tasker Settings' has a lower Target API, granting it access to a wider set of Android APIs." b:0,37
keep_existing_variables_help: Will only set the values of variables if they don't already exist by this point in the task
output_dates_format_help:
One or more date formats.

For example, yyyy/MM/dd HH:mm will produce a date like 2021/03/05 14:18

If you specify more than one output format, those formats will be applied to each input, so you'll have all the possible combinations of inputs and formats.

For example, if you have 2 inputs and 3 output formats, you'll get a total of 6 formatted values.

Check out all the possible formats below.
output_dates_format_variable_names_help:
One or more variable names.

Each output will be directly mapped to the variable name available here, e.g., output 1 > variable name 1, output 2 > variable name 2, etc.

Special Behavior for the Last Variable Name:
If there are more output formats than variable names, the last variable name on this list gets special treatment:
1. It will hold its directly mapped output value (e.g., if it's the 2nd variable name, it gets the 2nd output).
2. An array using the same name (e.g., %varname()) will also be created.
 • The first element of this array (%varname(1)) will be the same directly mapped value mentioned above.
 • Any subsequent formatted outputs (those that didn't have their own dedicated variable name) will populate the rest of the array (e.g., %varname(2), %varname(3), etc.).

Example:

Suppose you have 3 Output Formats:
1. dd-MM-yy
2. d
3. yyyy

And 2 Formatted Variable Names:
1. %date
2. %index_day

For an input date of 03-06-25 (assuming input format dd-MM-yy):
• %date (Variable 1) will be: 03-06-25 (from Output Format 1).
• %index_day (Variable 2, the last variable name) will be: 3 (from Output Format 2).
• %index_day() (the array for the last variable name) will contain:
 • %index_day(1) = 3 (from Output Format 2)
 • %index_day(2) = 2025 (from Output Format 3, the remaining unmapped output)
So, %index_day() effectively becomes an array like [3, 2025]." b:170,213 b:791,798 b:820,833 b:868,891
output_dates_help:
Since the input supports both single values and arrays you can use any of these outputs as both single values and arrays.

The number of outputs will depend on how many dates are input.

Additionally, for each Output Format more results will be added for the formated output.

For example, if you have 2 inputs and 3 output formats, you'll get a total of 6 values in the formatted variable output.
ppselect_configure_on_import_help: If you enable the option to configure on import you need to fill in a question that the user will be asked when importing this into Tasker. The value of this variable will also be cleared when you export it so that private data is not mistakenly sent to other users.
ppselect_text_profile_variables_help: The variables you add here will be available in the profile's conditions and tasks with the values you specify.
ppselect_text_project_variables_help: The variables you add here will be available in all the profiles and tasks in this project but will not be available in other projects.
ppselect_text_task_variables_help: The variables you add here will be available in this task, with the values you specify
profile_variable_export_value_help:
Under 'Exported Value' if you disable the 'Same as Value' option, you can customize what value gets exported when you share the variable with other users.
You can keep the 'Exported Value' field blank if you want the export to not have a value at all, or you can set the value you wish to always use for exports.
If you enable the 'Save as Value' option, the current variable value will be used when exporting.
profile_variable_immutable_help: If you enable the 'Immutable' option, the variable can be changed in Tasks, but will reset to the value here when the Task ends.
profile_variable_structured_output_help:
Enable the 'Structured Variable' option if the variable is either JSON, HTML or XML so that you can easily read its contents via the dot or square brackets notations.
For example if there's an %json variable and its contents are in the JSON format you could use '%json.info' or '%json[info]' to get the value for the 'info' field.
remote_timeout_help:
The maximum time to wait for the remote action to finish.

If set to 0, the task will continue right away and will not wait for the result.

If set to a positive number, Tasker will wait for the remote action to finish before moving on to the next action. Any local variables set by the remote action will be available in this task too.
settings_accessibility_help_usage_stats_:
If enabled will allow the accessibility service (if enabled) to also detect the current app, even if the App Check Method is set to 'Usage Stats'. This can make app detection faster in most situations, but might not always result in the intended results.

Keep this on if you don't see any anomalies in app detection because it's faster.
settings_action_error_notification_help: If enabled, every time an action ends in error you'll get notified about it unless the action has the 'Continue Task After Error' option enabled.
settings_ask_for_advanced_export_options: If enabled, every time you export a profile or task description, you can select some advanced formatting options for the output, like if it should wrap with backticks or use 4 spaces on every line instead.
settings_ask_for_permission_on_app_exit_:
If enabled, Tasker will check for all the necessary permissions when you exit the app from the main screen or save your setup.

Disable this setting if you have something in your setup that uses a permission that you don't want to remove, but don't want to grant permission for at the moment.
settings_debugging_use_test_servere_help:
If enabled will use a test server to share Tasker projects/profiles/tasks instead of Taskernet.

Use this to test out new server features when available.

If the tests server is offline you may get unexpected errors.
settings_export_light_help:
If enabled, your exports will not contain any data that is not essential for the correct functioning of your projects.

Some helpful info might go away like the names of local variables generated in actions/events/states in some situations, but that's just on the UI level. In the background all the necessary data is still kept.

This has the potential of greatly reducing the size of your backups and Tasker data in general.
settings_help_google_cloud_service_accou: Running actions remotely requires you to setup a Google Cloud and Firebase project.
settings_start_monitor_on_app_open_help: If enabled, as soon as you first open Tasker after a reboot, Tasker's monitor will start right away. If disabled, you'll need to exit Tasker or save your setup for the monitor to start.
structure_global_variable_help:
This variable seems to contain valid %1$s.

Did you know that you can access its contents easily and directly with Tasker?

Want to enable easy structure reading this for this variable now?
structure_prevent_json_smart_search_help: If enabled, Tasker will not automatically search the full JSON structure for the value when reading it.
structure_type_help:
Select the type of data that the variable contains.

If the type doesn't match the data when being read then the type 'None' is assumed instead.
tip_menu_help: You can press Menu then Info on most screens to access help.
user_handle_select_help:
You can select which profile to toggle by knowing the order you installed it on your device.

Unfortunately there's no way to show a label for each profile since Android doesn't provide it.

For example, if you first installed your Work Profile on your device and later you enabled Private Space, Work Profile will be the first (10) and Private Space will be the second (11).

By default, the first installed profile on your device will be toggled.
